statement: The function returns a result r. For an integer k >= 0, call a count vector c k-feasible when c assigns a nonnegative integer c(i) to every index 0 <= i < len(nums), the sum of all c(i) over 0 <= i < len(nums) equals k, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] - y*k - (x-y)*c(i) <= 0. Then r is the least nonnegative integer k for which a k-feasible count vector exists.
preconditions: len(nums) = n with 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= y < x <= 10^9.
